The facts, in short, are that the respondent No. 1 Syed Abedur Reza as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 97 of 1982 in the 1st Court of Munsif (now Assistant Judge) Sadar, Sylhet for declaring that the termination of the job of the said plaintiff as Senior Assistant in Uttara Bank was illegal, malafadie and without jurisdiction and that he was still in service of the Bank stating, inter-alia, that he joined the bank as Junior Assistant on 19.02.1977 in Sylhet Branch of Uttara Bank and his service was confirmed in the bank and following arrest of some Central leaders of the Bank Employees Federation, Dhaka on 09.09.1981 all the Bank Employees of the country went on strike as a mark of protest and so the plaintiff-respondent No.1 along with other staff of the Bank did not attend their job since 10.09.1981 and the bank management announced, through radio and television, a general amnesty to the striking employees declaring that in case of their joining duties by 24.09.1981 by 9 A. M. no action would be taken against them. Pursuant to the said announcement, the plaintiff-respondent joined his duty on 23.09.1981 at 9 A. M. but the defendant Nos. 5 and 2 did not allow him to join alleging that the plaintiff had already been terminated as per order of the defendant No. 2 and the plaintiff thereafter on 26.09.1981 received the impugned letter of termination of his service and hence he felt constrained to file the suit. 

3. The defendant-petitioner contested the suit filing a written statement denying material allegation made in the plaint sub-mitting, inter-alia, that the suit itself was not maintainable under Sections 4 and 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure and also under Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and that the plaintiff filed the suit in a wrong forum being an employee of a commercial bank, covered by the definition of "Worker" as defined in the Employment of Labour (Standing Orders) Act, 1965 and that the services of the plaintiff were not required by the bank and as such he was terminated as per provision of service rule of the bank and the order being a termination simplicity the plaintiff was entitled to get benefits admissible to him under the law. 

4. The learned Munsif (now Assistant Judge) after hearing the parties dismissed the suit by judgment and decree dated 18.02.1987. 

5. The plaintiff preferred Title Appeal No. 94 of 1987 before the learned District Judge, Sylhet. The learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), 1st Court, Sylhet by the judgment and order dated 22.03.1988 allowed the appeal and thereby decreed the suit. 

6. The defendant-petitioner moved the High Court Division under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and the High Court Division by the impugned judgment and order discharged the rule. 

7. It was submitted that the High Court Division as well as the lower appellate court failed to appreciate that the suit itself for a declaratory decree as to the illegality of the order dated 19.09.1981 for termination of the plaintiff from his service with-out any prayer for consequential relief was not maintainable in law in view of Section 42 of Specific Relief Act. The impugned decree passed by the lower appellate court declaring the termination of plaintiffs service as illegal and not binding on him and that the suit for declaration that he is still in service with the direction to allow him to continue in service in his post with all benefits, amounting to a mandatory injunction was not sustainable in law in view of the provisions of Section 21(a), (b) read with Section 56(f) and Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. Since the plain-tiffs' service was a contract of personal service and incapable of being specifically enforced and consequently, the plaintiffs suit ought to have been dismissed by the Courts below having regard to several reported decisions of this Court cited in the case, which are binding on the Court below, including the High Court Division, under Article III of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, which the High Court Division ignored with an observation that "the decisions cited from side of the defendant petitioner do not appear to have any bearing on the fundamental point which survives for determination in the suit". 

8. It was further submitted that the High Court Division fell in error in holding that the impugned termination order issued on 19.09.1981 under Rule 18(b) of the Bank's Staff Service Rules of 1965 being a dead service rule and dead law, the termination order is absolutely a nullity and without jurisdiction, in view of the fact that the petitioner bank on the date of issue of the order of termination of the plaintiff, had the power and was authorized to issue such order of termination of service under Rule 13 of Uttara Bank Service Regulation 1981 and although in the said termination order it was mentioned to be an order under rule 18(b) of the Bank's Staff Service Rules of 1965 it should be treated as an order under rule 13 of Uttara Bank Service Regulation 1981. This is because when the power of termination by the petitioner Ank-WAS inexistence in the rule of .1981, on 19.09.1981, a wrong quoting of the rule as rules of 1965 will not invalidate the order of termination itself and as such the High Court Division misconstrued the position of law and illegally discharged the rule and thereby confirmed the lower appellate court's direction to allow the plaintiff to continue in his post with all benefits which in fact amounts to a mandatory injunction in violation of the decision of this court in the case of Rupali Bank Vs. Arab Ali reported in 7 BLD(AD) at page-1. 

9. it was submitted that the Employment of Labour (Standing Orders) Act, 1965 provides appropriate relief in such matter to be had from the Labour Court and the plaintiff respondent No. 1 having filed the suit under the general jurisdiction of a Civil Court, without taking recourse to the Labour Court, a special forum provided for such relief, the suit was not maintain-able and as such non-consideration of the above aspect has rendered the judgment and decree as wholly illegal and bad in law. 

10. It was submitted that from the termination letter itself it stood revealed that as the service of the plaintiff was not required by the Bank his service was terminated which was a termination simplicity without any stigma with a direction to the plaintiff to obtain termination benefits and other dues from the concerned office and the termination of service with termination benefit cannot be termed as punishment and as such no notice need be served upon the plaintiff for passing the order of termination and the position being such, non-consideration of the above aspect rendered the impugned judgment and decree as wholly illegal and thus is liable to be set aside. 

11. It was submitted that although the defendant-petitioner has cited decisions reported in 40 DLR(AD) 45, 44 DLR(AD) 260 and 44 DLR (HCD) 589 in respect of the proposition that the plaintiff being an employee of a Commercial Establishment falls within the category of a "worker" as per definition of Section 2(v) of Employment of Labour (Standing Orders) Act, 1965 and as such his remedy lay before the Labour Court as per decisions referred to in 46 DLR (AD)1, 43 DLR(AD) 154 and 31 DLR (AD) 298. 

12. It was submitted that the show cause notice and/or principle of natural justice is not applicable in case of simple termination of any employee with all termination benefits and that in respect of the proposition that a 'person does not cease to be a worker merely on his designation but it depends on the nature of the job whether he is a worker or not and that a suit for declaration that the dismissal was illegal without asking for consequential relief for enforcing the declaratory decree and that non-consideration of the above decisions rendered the impugned judgment and decree as wholly illegal and bad .in law. 

13. It was lastly submitted that the decision of the High Court Division and decision that the decision of this court in the case of BSI Corporation Vs. Mahbub Hossain reported in 29 DLR (SC) 41 is still shining the path as the polestar to the adjudication of the issues regarding terms and conditions of employees of statutory .bodies is misconceived and not applicable °in the present case as it does not contemplate an action for reinstatement of a terminated employee in service with all benefits and hence the said observation does not support the present decision for con-firming the lower appellate court's decree for declaration as to the illegality of the plaintiffs termination from service or that he is still in service and a direction to allow him to continue in service with all benefits amounting to a mandatory injunction to put the plaintiff to the job of the bank again. 

14. Leave was granted to consider the above submissions. 

15. Heard Mr. Abdus Samad, the learned Counsel appearing for the appellant and Mr. Mahmudul Islam, the learned Counsel appearing for the respondents and perused the petition and the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division and other papers on record. 

16. The main contention of the learned Counsel appearing for the appellant is that the suit as frame was not maintainable against the termination order dated 19.09.1981 inasmuch as the respondent being a worker had his remedy before the labour court and not in a suit before the civil court. 

17. The respondent on the other hand submits that the proviso to Section 25(1) of the Act does not provide for the respondent any scope for lodging any complaint seeking any redress thereunder, as the order of termination of employment of the plaintiff, although made under Section 19 of the Act, was not passed for his trade union activities and did not deprive him of all the benefits specified in Section 19 of the Act i.e. Employment of Labour (Standing Orders) Act, 1965. 

18. In support of his contention the learned- Counsel for the respondent has referred to the case of Managing Director, Rupali Rank Limited Vs. Md. Nazrul Islam Patwary and others reported in 48 DLR(Ad) 62. 

19. It appears that the contention raised has been settled by this court in the afore-said decision and no further discussion is called for and accordingly the appeal is dismissed without any order as to cost. 

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Apple No. 2322 of 2008
lawyer:
Syed Haider Ali, Advocate, instructed by Syed Mahbubur Rahman, Advocate-On-Record ------ For the Petitioner 
Nurul Islam Bhuiya, Advocate-On-Record ------ For the Respondents
parties:
Arzoo Miah ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Abdur Rahim ------ Respondent
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated I 03.08.2008 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.2141 of 2001)
full_judgment:
Md. Muzammel Hossain J.: This petition for leave to appeal under Article 103 of the Constitution of Peoples' Republic of Bangladesh is directed against the judgment and order dated 03.08.2008 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.2141 of 2001 discharging the Rule upon affirming the judgment and decree dated 16.10.2000 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Dhaka in Title Appeal No.401 of 1999 affirming the judgment and decree dated 15.06.1999 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.196 of 1996 dismissing the suit.

2. The facts of the case, in brief, are that the petitioner as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No.196 of 1996 in the Court of Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka stating, inter-alia, that the late Mr. Batu Khan predecessors of the petitioner took lease of land measuring 1248 Ajutangsha from the Jaminder by paying proper salami and after his death his three sons Moti Khan, Hira Khan and Chunnu Khan become 16 (sixteen) anas owner of the suit property and thereafter of the permanent settlement of the suit land and on prayer Jaminder executed registered Kabulatnama in favour of Moti Khan, on 22.5.1907 as the said Moti Khan got Kabuliyat in respect of the suit property in his name, he and his two brothers namely Hira Khan, and Chunnu Khan, were also owning and possessing the same as per their share as inherited. During the C.S. operation the suit land was recorded in the name of Moti Khan, from the above three brothers. Hira Khan died leaving behind Lal kha as son and two daughters Paribanu, and Rehela died after the death of Hira Khan while they were unmarried. Chunnu Khan died leaving behind one wife Badrunnessa, three daughters namely, Hasan Banu, Bilkish Banu and Alder Banu, Akther Banu daughter of Badrunnessa, died unmarried leaving behind her two nieces Hasan Banu, Bilkish Banu as her heirs and uncle Moti Khan, her Hira Lal Khan only son of Hira Khasn had married Sakhina Banu and started living in that house in suit land. Sakhina Banu gave birth to Lal Khan's four legitimate sons and 5 daughters. Lal Khan died on 1943 leaving them behind as heirs. The recorded owner Moti Khan aged about 90, died unmarried and leaving Lal Khan son of Hira Khan, Hossain Banu and Bilkish Banu heirs of her brother Chunnu Khan as heirs to his left off properties Chunnu Khan gave marriage of his daughter Bilkish Banu with Bacchu Miah during his life. Arzoo Miah was the only legitimate son of Bacchu Miah, Bacchu Miah took charge of the family of late Chunnu Khan as he died without any son. Heirs of Chunnu Khan and Kim Khan for their convenience constructed semi puma house proportioning the 1248 Ajutangsha suit property among them. Among the 4 sons of Lal Khan, the plaintiff No, 2 is still alive and his 5 daughters have been living with their husbands. Sakhina died later.

3. Sakhina and her sons constructed a room pucca building with a Kitchen and a bedroom out of Joint fund with Bacchu Miah and Bilkish Banu and they equally enjoying owning and possessing the same house through tenants. Bacchu Miah being the oldest and acknowledged person was given the Liability of managing the 1248 Ajutangsha of the suit property and the pucca and semi pucca house on it. In January, 1992 defendant was evicted from his former house and pledged for a shelter as he along with his family was totally shelter less. Thereafter the defendant pledged through the local leaders Md. Ismail, Golam Muhammad and Kalachand Bepary for a temporary shelter as in that house in suit which was vacant. After that they denied to leave the house within one month. That is how the defendant took possession of the house along with his family in January, 1992.

4. Bacchu Miah had become seriously ill due to old age complication and informed the local community leaders that the defendant was not leaving the possession. Thereafter the defendant pledged for another month and he agreed.

5. On 13.05.92 Bacchu Miah passed away and the defendant were still in possession. Defendant No. 1 informed it towards the neighbors community. Defendant being pressurized agreed to leave the possession within the last of May, 1992. Observing the unwillingness of leaving plaintiff along with local leaders told the defendant to leave the property. But the defendant did not to leave the property and hand over the same to the plaintiff and the plaintiff tiled the suit praying for ejectment of the defendant from the suit property as licensee.

6. The defendant-respondent contested the suit by filing written statements stating, inter-alia, that Moti Khan, Chunnu Khan sons of Batuki were the owners of the 1248 Ajutangsha of the suit property. Moti Khan died childless, leaving his nephews and nieces as his heirs.

7. Thus Lal Khan sons of Hira Khan and his heirs Sakina Bewa, Osman Goni, Abdul Barek, Abdul Khalek, Abdul Malek, Nazneen Begum, Nanni Begum, Azmiri Begum and Ayesha Khatun, become the owners of the property. Hassen Banu, daughter of Chunnu Khan presented the property orally to Bacchu Miah. In need of money, Sakina Bewa, Osman Goni, Abdul Barek, Abdul Khalek, Nazneen Behum, Nazneen Begum, Azmiri Begum decided to sell .0248 Ajutangsha of the suit property in 1978.

8. According to a proposal of Tk. 12,000/ for that property Bilkish Banu and Bacchu Miah sold of their portion at Tk. 6,000/- and Sakina Bewa, Osman Goni, Abdul Barek, Abdul Khaleque, Nazneen Begum, Nance Begum, Azmiri Begum, Amena Khatun and Ayesha Khatun also received Tk. 6000/-(Six thousand) for their portion and handed over the possession to the defendant and his wife. Thereafter a map of the sold and remaining properties was prepared, showing every body's portions separately. Bacchu Miah and Bilkish Banu signed and tipped respectively on that map. Sakhina Bewa and Abdul Khaleque did the same in favour of the other party. Thereafter the defendant constructed brick wall and building on the periphery of land. The sellers failed to hand over the title deed, thereafter defendant summons the sell deed. Then on 22.12.79 Bacchu Miah, Bilkish Banu, Osman Goni, A. Barek, A. Khaleque (plaintiff No. 2) A. Malek, Nazneen Begum, Nanne Begum, Azmiri Begum, Amena Khatun, Ayesha Khatun, admitted to hair received Tk.12,000/- and promised the completion and registration of the deed within a month. Father of the plaintiff along with all sellers signed in that agreement Because of the deed of agreement plaintiff’s case is barred by the section 53(4) of Transfer of Property. These defendants have been paying the City Corporation tax, opening a holding in his name in Dhaka Municipal Corporation. The defendant also has been paying gas bill and electricity bill after having been connected. The defendant constructed a building in the suit property. Thus this defendant being the owner of the suit property, have been living there for more than 12 years and that is how the defendant also got the right of adverse possession. As there exist another case concerning the suit property the sellers were unable to complete the execution and registration of the deed. In the meantime Osman Goni, Abdul Barek, Abdul Malek, Bacchu Miah, and Bilkish Banu passed away. It is to be mentioned that, plaintiff No. 1 is the son of Bacchu Miah and Bilkish Banu. This defendant is not a licensee of the plaintiff. Therefore the defendant pledged dismissed of the suit.

9. The learned Senior Assistant Judge, Dhaka by the judgment and decree 15.06.1999 dismissed the suit by contest Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree the plaintiff-petitioner preferred Title Appeal No.401 of 1999 in the Court of Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka who by the judgment and decree dated 16.10.2000 dismissed the appeal affirming those passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge.

10. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree dated 16.10.2000 the plaintiff-petitioner preferred revisional application before the High Court Division being Civil Revision No.2141 of 2001 in which the Rule was discharged by a Single Bench of the High Court Division by the judgment and order dated 03.08.2008. Thereafter the petitioner preferred the instant civil petition for leave to appeal before the Appellate Division.

<u>11. We have heard Mr. Syed Haider Ali, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner and Mr. Nurul Islam Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate-On-Record appearing for the respondent, perused the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division and all other connected papers on record. It appears that the High Court Division on consideration of the materials on record and having gone through the judgment and decree of the courts below observed that both the courts below found that the owners of the property of the suit land having decided to sell the same to the defendant respondent and his wife at Tk. 12,000/- and handed over the vacant possession of the property to them. But the owner of the property the predecessors of the plaintiff-petitioner handed over the possession of the suit property to the defendant respondent but the deed of sale could not be executed and registered rather they executed a deed of agreement for sale admitting the receipt of entire considerations of money of Tk. 12,000/- and handed over the possession of the property. The defendant-respondents having received the possession of the property raised pucca construction and partition wall in the said property. It has also admitted by the plaintiff petitioner that the defendant and his wife opened a different Municipal Holding No.128/A in their names and the High Court Division noticed that both the Court below made concurrent findings of fact that the defendant-petitioner has been in possession of holding No.128/A paying the Municipal rents regularly since 1983 and they also took gas connection in the property in 1980, electric connection was also taken and paying the bills regularly. The defendant made two storied building in 1981 on the suit property and he has been possessing the same for more than 12 years. So adverse right had been approved to them. The High Court Division observed that both the courts below made concurrent findings of fact that the defendant paid rents, was a bills and other utility services for the suit land. The mandatory provision of Section 17 of the Registration Act was not complied with as the alleged Bainapatra Exbt. Ka was not registered. But such unregistered documents was given protection under Section 53A of the, Transfer of Property Act. Relying on the provision of Section 53A of the Transfer of Poverty Act the High Court Division referred to the case of Mir Abdul -Vs- Md. Rafiqul Islam reported in 8 BLD (AD) 149 and the decision reported in 16 DLR (SCD) 1969. High Court Division rightly held that since the defendant is possessing and owning in the property for more than 12 years he had acquired adverse right and title on the suit property. In the case of Mir Abdul -Vs-Md. Rafiqul Islam reported in 8 BLD (AD) 149 the Appellate Division held that when on the showing of the plaintiff himself the defendant was in possession of the suit land in furtherance of his bainapatra. The equitable principle as given in Section 53A of the Transfer of the Property Act can be invoked by the defendant for protecting his possession.</u>

12. In the instant case High Court Division noticed that both the courts below rightly found that on the basis of the agreement to sell the suit property the defendant has been possessing the property for more than 12 years and they have developed the suit property by constructing houses and erecting walls and they have been paying rents, wasa bills and all other utility services.

13. Having made the aforesaid observation the High Court Division rightly found that the court of appeal below committed no error of law in passing the judgment and decree dismissing the appeal and thereby concurring with the decision of those passed by the trial court in dismissing the suit.

14. In view of the above facts and circumstances we are of the view that the High Court Division upon correct assessment of materials on record arrived at a correct decision and thus we do not find any merit in the leave petition.

15. Accordingly, the leave petition is dismissed.

End.

lawyer:
A.Y. Ahmed Ali Sarder, Advocate, instructed by Md. Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Appellants
Mahmudul Islam, Senior Advocate, instructed by Md. Abu Siddique, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Respondents
parties:
Md. Ismail Hossain Sarker and others ------ Appellants
Vs.
Khushi Mohan Mondal and Ors. ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the Judgment and Order dated 17.01.2004 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2807 of 1999)
full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hossain, J. This appeal by leave by the defendant-appellants is directed against the judgment and order dated January 17, 2004 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2807 of 1999 discharging the Rule affirming the judgment and decree dated April 25, 1999 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Second Court, Tangail in Other Class Appeal No. 148 of 1998 reversing the judgment and decree dated June 29, 1998 passed by the then learned Subordinate Judge, Third Court, Tangail in Title Suit No. 251 of 1994 dismissing the same. The facts, leading to the filing of this appeal, in a nutshell are:

<u>2. Respondent No. 1 herein as the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 251 of 1994 in the Court of the then Subordinate Judge, Third Court, Tangail for declaration of title in respect of the suit land described in the schedule to the plaint. His case, in short, is that the plaintiff claimed the land in suit on the basis of deed of gift. The land in suit has been wrongly recorded in the names of defendant Nos. 1-12 and 14-32. The defendants have never possessed the property in suit and they had never taken settlement and the plaintiff came to know about the preparation of the wrong record of right on December 16, 1989 and as the same wrong record has clouded his title, the plaintiff was strained to file the suit for declaration of his title in the suit land.</u>

3. Defendant No. 1 and 35-37 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material statements made in the plaint. Their case, in short, is that the suit was barred by limitation and was bad for defect of parties and that the Dhaka Nawab Waqf Estate and Karatia Waqf Estate were the superior landlords, Gangadhar Namadas and his brothers were the tenants and they having defaulted in the payment of rent, their tenancy was sold in auction in a proceeding of 1933-1934 and the said tenancy was purchased by the Dhaka Nawab Waqf Estate. The land of the said tenancy along with other lands was settled to Momtazuddin, Abdul Quddus, Abdul Hakim, Intaz Ali and Abdul Hai. By amicable settlement Intaz Ali got land of plot Nos. 3146 and 3174 and he died leaving behind defendant No. 1 and three daughters (defendant Nos. 35-37) and defendant No. 1 by two deeds gave 91 decimals of land to his sisters. Defendant Nos. 1 and 35-37 were in possession of the suit land. The plaintiff has no right, title and interest in the suit plot Nos. 3146 and 3174 or in other words in the suit land.

4. The trial Court upon hearing the parties by the judgment and order dated 29.06.1998 dismissed the suit on the findings that the plaintiff had no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land and the plaintiff had failed to establish his claim in respect of the suit land.

5. Against the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the plaintiff preferred Other Class Appeal No. 148 of 1998 before the learned District Judge, Tangail. On transfer, the appeal was heard and disposed of by the learned Additional District Judge, Second Court, Tangail, who by his judgment and order dated 25.04.1999 allowed the appeal reversing the judgment and decree of the trial Court.

6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the appellate Court, the defendants moved the High Court Division by filing a revisional application and obtained Rule in Civil Revision No. 2807 of 1999.

7. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division upon hearing the parties by the judgment and order dated 17.04.2004 discharged the Rule.

8. Feeling aggrieved by and dissatisfied with judgment and order passed by the High Court Division, the defendants moved this Division by filing Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos. 412 of 2005 and leave was granted on 10.08.2006 resulting in Civil Appeal No. 126 of 2006.

9. Mr. A.Y. Ahmed Ali Sarder, learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the appellants, submits that the High Court Division erroneously concurred with the findings of the appellate Court that the plaintiff could prove his title to and possession of the suit land without at all the finding arrived at by the trial Court as regards title of the plaintiff and as such, the impugned judgment should be set aside. He further submits that the appellants could prove that in fact, the suit land along with other lands was sold in auction and that their predecessors-in-interest, namely, Entaz Ali, Abdul Hakim and others took settlement of 5.79 acres of land of the suit khatian on payment of salami and that all the Courts below erroneously came to the finding that the defendants could not prove the alleged auction and as such, the impugned judgment should be set aside. The learned Advocate also submits that the plaintiff created a forged deed of gift dated 28.07.1985 and that the said deed was registered in a different Sub-Registry office by incorporating .01 acre of fictitious land in order to attract jurisdiction of that Sub-Registry office and as such, the deed of gift is void.

10. Mr. Mahmudul Islam, learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-respondent, on the other hand, submits that the appellate Court being the final Court of fact on proper appreciation of the evidence on record came to a finding that the plaintiff could prove his title to and possession in the suit land and that the High Court Division correctly found that the appellate Court was justified in arriving such finding and as such, no interference is called for.

11. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocate of both the sides, perused the impugned judgment and the materials on record.

12. It is necessary to go through the grounds, on which leave was granted and the grounds are quoted below:

"The appellate Court as well as the High Court Division has failed to arrive at a decision to the effect that the plaintiff failed to prove his case in the light of the decisions reported in 24 DLR 274 and 39 DLR (AD) 237. The High Court Division and the Court of appeal have failed to avert to the findings and observation as manifested in the judgment of the trial Court passed in Other Suit No. 251 of 1994 dismissing the suit and as such the impugned judgments are not proper judgments of reversal in the background of the decisions reported in 1997 BLT (AD) 15 and 37 DLR 93 placing reliance on the decisions reported in 1960 (SC) 115, AIR 1951 (SC) 120 and also 34 DLR (AD) 52."

13. Admittedly, the suit land belonged to Gangadhar Namadas, Nedu Namadas and Nagarbashi Namadas and accordingly, the C.S. Khatian was correctly prepared and published in their names. According to the plaintiff, C.S. recorded tenant, Nagarbashi Namadas died unmarried and as such, his share was inherited by his two full brothers. Gangadhar Namadas sold .35 acre of land out of his share to Shahed Ali and Raj Ali, the predecessors-in-interest of defendant Nos. 2-6, and died leaving behind only daughter Rajeshwari Namadas. The transfer of Gangadhar Namadas to the predecessors-in-interest of defendant Nos. 2-6 was proved by production of relevant volume from the office of the Sub-Registrar, Tangail by PW. 6. The plaintiffs claimed that defendant No. 33 Rajeshwari had no male child and that in the absence of her husband her share was inherited by her uncle's four sons, namely, Khushi Mohan (the plaintiff), Shamvu Charan Mondal, Makhon Mondal and Nani Gopal Mondal. The plaintiffs also claimed that C.S. recorded tenant Nedu Namadas die leaving behind four sons including the plaintiff. The plaintiff asserted that by amicable partition amongst me brothers, he got 3.04 acres of land out of the suit land. The plaintiffs claimed that his brothers transferred their interest in the suit land to him by a registered deed of gift dated 28.03.1985. The plaintiffs produced the original deed of gift (exhibit-2). Having considered the evidence on record, the appellate Court came to a finding that the plaintiff could prove his title to, and possession in the suit land.

<u>14. On the other hand, the defendant claimed that the suit land along with other lands was sold in auction. In order to prove the certificate sale, the defendants could not produce the sale certificate and writ of delivery of possession. The trial Court found the defendants could not produce certificate copies of the shelf-index and the sale certificate and in the absence of those important documents, it could be not said that the suit land was sold in auction and as a result, the right, title and interest of C.S. recorded tenants were not extinguished in the suit land. The defendants further claimed that their predecessors-in-interest, Entaz Ali, Abdul Hakim and others obtained lease of 5.79 acres of land of the suit khatian. In order to prove the settlement, the defendants produced exhibit-F/14. The trial Court found that those receipts showing payment of salami did not prove that Entaz Ali, Abdul Hakim, Momtaz Ali Abdul Quddus and Abdul Hye got settlement and possession in the suit land. The trial Court, the appellate Court and the High Court Division concurrently found that the defendants could not prove the alleged auction in support of their claim to suit land.</u>

<u>15. The plaintiffs stated that he acquired title of his three brothers in the suit land as they executed and registered a deed of gift dated 28.03.1985 in his favour in respect of their interest in the suit land. Admittedly, at the relevant time, the three brothers of the plaintiffs had no land in Mirzapur Police station but in order to attract Jurisdiction of Mirzapur Sub-Registry office .01 acre of land out of .13 acre of land of Plot No. 1522 of Gajeshwary Mouza of Mirzapur Police Station was included in the said deed of gift dated 28.07.1985. The trial Court correctly came to the finding that because of inclusion of fictitious land the deed of gift was void.</u>

<u>16. In this connection, reliance may be placed on the case of Syed Kawshar Ali Vs. Gahar Kazi and others (1985) 37 DLR 177, in which, this Division noticed with approval of the decision of the Bombay High Court report in AIR 1954 Bombay at page 54 and quoted as under:</u>

<u>"Various circumstances may arise in case of unwarranted inclusion of property in a deed. For instance, a property may not in fact exits at all and still be included to enable registration being effected in a particular place and may be a fictitious inclusion in that sense. In such a case registration is invalid: 1914 P.C. 67 (15); Secondly, the property may exist, but the grantor has no title to it, and neither party to the deed intends to include it as a fact as a subject matter of the deed. In such a case also registration is invalid: 1921 P.C. (16); Thirdly, the property exists but is not proved to belong to the grantor and still there is a bonafide belief at least on the part of the grantee that it belong to the grantor. In such a case registration is not invalid, and the burden is on the party challenging the validity to prove that the inclusion of the property was intended to be fictitious by both the parties: 1919 All 450 (19), 1924 All, 897 (20) and observations in 1921 P.C. 8(16)."</u>

<u>17. Having considered the quoted portion of the above judgment, we are of the view that because of inclusion of property in the deed of gift not belonging to the brothers of the plaintiff, the deed of gift is void. The aforesaid .01 acre of land was included in the deed of gift in order to attract jurisdiction of Sub-Registry office of Mirzapur. Since the deed of gift standing in the name of the plaintiff is void and the plaintiff is not entitled to get a decree.</u>

Accordingly, the appeal is allowed without any order as costs.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 45 of 2010
lawyer:
Bishmodeb Chakraborty, Deputy Attorney General, instructed by Mr. B. Hossain, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioners 
For Respondents Not represented.
parties:
Upazilla Nirbahi Officer and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Abdul Kadir Mia and others ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 23rd of April, 2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1036 of 2007)
full_judgment:
Mohammad Imman Ali, J. This Civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 23.04.2009 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1036 of 2007 discharging the Rule. The facts of the case, in brief, are that the respondent No. 1 as plaintiffs instituted suit for declaration of his title in the land in dispute claiming that .72 acre of land appertaining to C.S. Khatian No. 228, plot No. 123 of Mouza Kashinagar, under Police Station-Nandail, District-Mymensingh belonged to Barkot Mondol of which the C.S. Record was prepared in the name of his son Ekdil Mondol. The S.A. Record in respect of the said land was prepared in the name of Abdul Aziz, Hafiz Uddin and Shahed Ali. After death of S.A. recorded tenant Shahed Ali his son Bacchu Miah sold .02 acre of land of disputed plot No. 125 to the plaintiff by executing a kabala dated 04.04.2001. Former Zaminder Gyanda Sundari Chowdhury, the C.S. recorded Malik as its owner and possessor settled .01 acre out of .88 acre of land of disputed plot No. 124 with the plaintiff and his brother whereon they have been running their business by constructing huts. The said .01 acre settled with them was recorded in their names in S.A. Khatian No. 222, one Yousuf Ali also took settlement of .02 acre of plot No. 124 from the said Zaminder and while he had been in enjoyment and possession sold the same to the plaintiff by executing a kabala dated 06.07.1960 before preparation of the S.A. record which was wrongly prepared in the name of Yousuf Ali. In such manner he (plaintiff) has been enjoying and possessing .02 acre in plot No. 125 and .01 1/2 acre in plot No. 124, in total .03 1/2 acre, and it was mutated in his name and he has been enjoying and possessing the same paying rent to the Government. Out of .88 acre of land of plot No. 124, .82 acre was wrongly recorded in Khas Khatian No. 1 and the remaining .06 acre was recorded in the names of different persons including him. The land of disputed plot No. 124 is situated in Khaligonj Bazar. There is a Mahogany Tree in his land in plot No. 125 and in the same plot the Kaligonj Jame Masjid is situated. For renovation of his huts he used a branch of his said tree and at that time the surveyor of local land office demanded bribe from him. Being refused, the surveyor instituted a false criminal case against him and others. Earlier he filed other class Suit No. 97 of 2002 in respect of the same land, but for some formal defects that suit was withdrawn with permission to sue afresh. The defendants threatened to dispossess him from the suit land on 21.12.2002.

2. The defendant Government contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations claiming that .82 acre of land out of .88 acre in plot No. 124 was recorded in Khatian No. 1 and the record in respect of the remaining .06 acre was prepared in the names of different persons namely Abdul Hamid and Moqbul Hossain in respect of .02 acre in Khatian No. 219, Abdul Hafiz in respect of .02 acre in Khatian No. 212, Yousuf Ali in respect of .01 acre in Khatian No. 220, Besides that S.A. Khatian No. 220 in respect of .44 acre of disputed plot No. 125 was prepared in the name of Abdul Aziz, S.A. Khatian No. 227 in respect of .20 acre of disputed plot No. 125 was prepared in the name of Ismail, S.A. Khatian No. 230 in respect of .04 acre of plot No. 125 was prepared in the name of Akhter Hussain on behalf of the Mosque and S.A. Khatian No. 231 in respect of .04 acre of land of plot No. 125 was prepared in the name of Aftab Ali. As per the Government policy the plaintiff was evicted from the suit land by demolishing his huts thereon. In .82 acre of land of plot No. 124 the Union Land Office is situated Earlier on the plaintiff instituted another suit in respect of the same land and finding no scope of success withdrew that suit and instituted the instant suit with false claim which is liable to be dismissed.

3. After hearing the parties the leaned Senior Assistant Judge, Nandail, Mymensingh, by his judgment and decree dated 22.8.2005 dismissed the suit.

4. Against the said judgment and decree passed by the trial court the plaintiff preferred Other Class Appeal No. 191 of 2005 before the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Mymensingh who upon hearing the parties and considering the materials on record allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial court.

5. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and decree the defendant No. 1 Upazila Nirbahi Officer, Nandail, Mymensingh as petitioner preferred civil revision No. 1036 of 2007 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule. By the impugned Judgment and order the High Court Division discharged the Rule. Hence the defendant No. 1 and others as petitioners have filed the instant civil petition for leave to appeal before this Division.

6. Mr. Bishmodeb Chakraborty, learned Deputy Attorney General appearing on behalf of the petitioners submitted that the suit of the plaintiff was not maintainable without a prayer for partition, which was correctly found by the trial court after proper discussion of the evidence and materials on record. However, that finding of the trial Court was erroneously reversed by the appellate Court without proper discussion. As such the High Court Division has erred in law in discharging the Rule. He further submitted that documents exhibited at the trial without formal objection shall not necessarily be treated as admitted documents and, therefore, the appellate Court erred in decreeing the suit of the plaintiff on the basis of documents exhibited and the High Court Division erred in discharging the Rule. Learned D.A.G. also submitted that the plaintiff had previously instituted another suit in respect of the same land and finding no scope of success withdrew that suit, thereafter filing the instant suit with a false claim, but the High Court Division did not at all discuss that point.

7. No one has appeared for the respondent.

8. We have considered the submissions of the learned Deputy Attorney General and perused the impugned judgment and other connected papers on record.

<u>9. We note from the judgment of the appellate Court that it came to a finding that the claim of the plaintiff regarding 1 decimal of land of plot No. 124 and 2 decimal of land of plot No. 125 is supported by documents marked as Exhibit-3, 3(Ka), 3(Kha), 6 and 9 and the plaintiff also submitted some rent receipts (exhibit-5 series) which supported the plaintiffs claim that he had paid rent for the suit property after getting the same mutated in his name. The appellate Court also found that the plaintiffs claim was supported by the evidence of P.W. Nos. 2, 3, 4 and 5 regarding possession of the suit property.</u>

<u>10. The High Court Division found that plaintiffs land was specifically disclosed in the plaint mentioning the plot numbers. Khatian numbers and quantum of land giving boundary and sketch map stating the manner of possession. The High Court Division also noted that the Government claim chat the suit land became Khas under the Government was not supported by any proof of transmission of ownership from the former landlord to the Government.</u>

<u>11. We do not find any illegality or infirmity in the decision given by the High Court Division. The impugned judgment does not call for any interference by this Division.</u>

Accordingly, this Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal is dismissed.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for leave to Appeal No. 1037 of 2011
lawyer:
Mahbubey Alam, Attorney General, instructed by Md. Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner 
Rokanuddin Mahmud, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mr. Bivash Chandra Biswas, Advocate-on-Record ------ For Respondent No.1 
Respondent Nos.2-3 ------ Not represented.
parties:
The Managing Director, Biman Bangladesh Airlines ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Syed Khwaza Jonaid and others ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 31.01.2011 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 7689 of 2010)
full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hossain J. This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 31.01.2011 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 7689 of 2010 making the Rule absolute.

2. The facts leading to the filing of this petition for leave to appeal, in short, are:

3. The petitioner was appointed as an Instructor (Flight Service) in the Ground Training Center in Pay Group-VI in the erstwhile Bangladesh Biman Corporation, vide appointment letter dated 01.01.1982. Upon further selection by Biman, he was re-designated as a Commercial Officer, vide letter dated 19.09.1985. The petitionor was successively promoted to the posts of Assistant Manager (Commercial), Manager (Commercial) Deputy General Manager (Commercial) and finally he was retired as General Manager. On promotion, the petitioner was successively posted as, amongst others, Market Research Officer, Sales Promotion Officer, Manager (Passenger Sales), Country Manager for Greece and Cyprus based in Athens in 1990-1993, Country Manager for Germany and Poland based in Frankfurt in 1993-1995, Manager (Market Research), Country Manager for Singapore, Brunei and Australia based in Singapore in 1997-1998, General Manager in UK, Ireland and Spain based in London in 1998-2001, Regional Manager in Dubai and Northern Emirates based in Dubai in 2002-2004, Deputy General Manager (Marketing), General Manager (Marketing), General Manager (District Sales), General Manager (Sales) and Director (Acting) Marketing and Sales before finally posted as General Manager (Cargo). While posted in Athens, he was able to increase Biman's revenue by 37% and obtain off line business for Biman from Cyprus. While the petitioner was posted in Germany, Biman's flight frequency to Germany increased. During his tenure in London, Biman's frequency increased to daily flights and also flights between London and Sylhet commended. As a member of Biman's Head Office delegations, the petitioner negotiated and concluded agreements with British Airways, Kuwait Airways, Emirates, Singapore Airlines, Iran Air and Uzbekistan Airways. In appreciation of his continuous good service, the petitioner was issued lettern of appreciation by his superiors, including letters dated 19.09.1982, 28.11.2005 and an undated letter specifically mentioning that because of the aggressive marketing strategies, Human revenue in UK increased substantially. In the normal course of his service, the petitioner was due to retire on 25.03.2015, having been born on 26.03.1958, upon attaining the age of superannuation of 57 years. The petitioner completed 25 years of service in January, 2007. All of a sudden he received the impugned letter dated 16.09.2010 (Annexure-A of the writ petition) prematurely retiring him from service on completion of his 25 years of service with effect from 19.09.2010 under regulation 11A (2) of the Bangladesh Biman Corporation Employees (Service) Regulations, 1979 (in short, the service regulations), which was inserted by way of an amendment, vide notification dated 05.02.1984. The notice dated 13.09.2010 was issued for holding 67th meeting of the Board of Directors of Biman on 15.09.2010 with only two specific agendas, namely, confirmation of the minimum of 66th Board Meeting and reports of different committees. At the 67th Board Meeting held on 15.09.2010 (Annexure-B of the writ petition) a resolution was included under the "Miscellaneous Agenda" resolving to retire the petitioner from service under regulation 11A (2) of the service regulations upon the predication "that in order to instill discipline and re-invigorate the commercial activities it was imperative to bring immediate changes in the higher management". Curiously enough there was no upending for considering the service of the petitioner. On the same plea, a colleague of the petitioner was terminated from service under regulation 52(1) of the service regulations. The petitioner has never been issued any notice asking him to show cause as to why any action, disciplinary or otherwise, should not be taken against him alleging that any act or omission caused by him resulted in lack of discipline and/or lack or vigour in commercial activities in Biman for which it was necessary to retire him prematurely, despite the fact that the predication of the impugned resolution, i.e. "to instil discipline and re-invigorate the commercial activities" reclarly stigmatizes and casts an aspersion on the petitioner.

4. Challenging the memo dated 16.09.2010 and the resolution No.3.1.b dated 15.09.2010 passed at 67th meeting of the Board of Directors of writ respondent No.1 under agenda No.3 retiring the writ petitioner from service, the writ petitioner obtained the Rule Nisi.

5. Respondent Nos.1 and 2 filed an affidavit-in-opposition controverting the statements made in the writ petition. Their case, in short, is that Regulation 11A(2) provides for retirement from service of an employee after completion of 25 years of service if the Corporation considers it expedient to do so and as such the petitioner has rightly been retired from service in exercise of aforesaid power of the Bangladesh Biman Corporation Employees (Service) Regulations, 1979.

6. The High Court Division made the Rule absolute after hearing both the parties and declared the memo dated 19.06.2010 to have been passed without lawful authority by the judgment and order dated 31.01.2011.

7. Feeling aggrieved by the judgment and order dated 31.01.2011 passed by the High Court Division, writ-respondent No.2 has filed this Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal.

8. We have perused the petition and the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division and other papers on record.

9. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner herein, submits that the instant writ petition having been decided by the High Court Division relying upon the decision reported in 13 MLR (AD) 1, (decided on 03.09.2007) interpreting the scope of regulation 11 A(2) of the Bangladesh Biman Corporation (Service) Regulations, 1979 and in deciding the said case this Division having not considered an earlier decision of this Division reported in 10 BLT (AD) 22 (decided on 22.05.2000) on the same regulation in which a contrary view has been taken, the matter is required to be finally decided by this Division.

10. He further submits that Biman having been made a limited company from Corporation with effect from 31.07.2007, the High Court Division erred in not taking into consideration the said fact in deciding the applicability of regulation 11A(2) of the Bangladesh Biman Corporation (Service) Regulation 1979 in respect its officers and employees.

11. Mr. Rokanuddin Mahmud learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf of writ-petitioner submits that regulation 11A (2) having been incorporated in the service regulations on 05.04.1984 shall not apply to petitioner who was admittedly appointed on 01.01.1982 and as such, the petition for leave should be dismissed.

12. The submissions made on behalf of the petitioner merit consideration.

<u>13. Therefore, leave is granted to consider the following points:</u>

<u>1. Whether the instant writ petition having been decided by the High Court Division relying upon the decision reported in 13 MLR (AD) 1, (decided on 03.09.2007) interpreting the scope of regulation 11A(2) of the Bangladesh Biman Corporation (Service) Regulations, 1979 and in deciding the said ease this Division having not considered an earlier decision of this Division reported in 10 BLT (AD) 22 (decided on 22.05.2000) on the same regulation in which a contrary view has been taken, the matter is required to be finally decided by this Court.</u>

<u>2. Whether Biman having been made a limited company from Corporation with effect from 31.07.2007, the High Court Division erred in not taking into consideration the said fact in deciding the applicability of regulation 11A(2) of the Bangladesh Biman Corporation (Service) Regulations 1979 in respect its officers and employees.</u>

<u>3. Whether regulation 11A (2) having been incorporated in the service regulations on 05.04.1984 shall apply to the writ petitioner who was admittedly appointed on 01.01.1982.</u>

14. Preparation of the paper book is dispensed with as prayed for.

15. The petitioner is permitted to add additional grounds.

16. The order of stay, granted earlier extended for 3(three) months.

17. The appellant is directed to make the appeal ready by 10.07.2011 and 1(one) week thereof for the respondent to file the concise statement positively.

18. The appeal comes up for hearing in list on 27th July, 2011.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2281 of 2011
lawyer:
Mahmudul Islam, Senior Advocate, Probir Neogi, Advocate, instructed by Md. Taufique Hossain, Advocate-on-Record ------- For the Petitioner
Rokanuddin Mahmud, Syed Aminul Islam, Senior Advocates and Khaliur Rahman, Advocate, instructed by Md. Zahirul Islam, Advocate-on-Record ------- For the Respondent No. 1.
Nurul Islam Bhuiyan, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Respondent No. 39.
For Respondent Nos. 2-38 & 40-43 ------ Not Represented.
parties:
Md. Khorshed Alam ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Md. Shahidullah and others ----- Respondents
case_source: (From the Judgment and Decree dated 7.6.2011 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4190 of 2010)
full_judgment:
Surendra Kumar Sinha, C.J. The dispute in this petition is in respect of .02 acre of land out of .65 acre of C.S. plot No. 125 of C.S. Khatian No. 53 corresponding to S.A. Khatian No. 53/2 under Mohammadpur Police Station as described in schedule 'Kha' to the plaint and the parties have been litigating over the subject matter more than 23 years after passing of the preliminary decree in the suit instituted in 1989. There is chequered history in this matter, which shakes the very foundation of our justice delivery system. The suit is for partition in which the plaintiff claimed a saham of .32 acre of land out of .65 acre of land of schedule 'Ka' to the plaint on the strength of a registered deed dated 8th June, 1936 with a declaration that the defendant Nos. 1-5 have no right, title and interest in respect of schedule 'Kha' land with a prayer for recovery of possession of .02 acre of land out of .65 acre, on the ground that he has been dispossessed by the defendant No. 1 in pursuance of a collusive decree passed in Title Suit No. 75 of 1985.

2. Short facts relevant for the disposal of the matter are that 1.35 acres land of C.S. Plot No. 125 appertaining to C.S. Khatian No. 53 of Mouza 248 Gajmahal, P.S. Dhanmondi along with lands of C.S, Plot Nos. 124, 125, 130 and 133 of C.S. Khatian No. 53 originally belonged to Sk. Dilbar, who died leaving behind his two sons Alimuddin and Nizamuddin and a daughter Maleka Bibi. Alimuddin sold his entire share to his brother Nizamuddin in 1931 by a registered sale deed. Thereafter, Maleka Bibi by an amicable partition with her brother Nizamuddin got .72 acre of C.S. Plot No. 133 in her exclusive 'saham' and Nizamuddin got the remaining land of that plot and plot No. 125 with an area of 1.35 acres in his exclusive 'saham'. On 8th June, 1936 Nizamuddin sold .65 acre land of C.S. Plot No. 125 to Chuni Jamadar and remained in possession of the remaining .70 acre of the said plot. Plaintiff is claiming the saham on the basis of seccessive transfers from Nizamuddin's share and amicable partition. According to the plaintiff, the defendant No. 1 in collusion with defendant No. 3 filed T.S. No. 75 of 1985 under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act with a view to evicting him from his land and obtained a decree on 17th August, 1989 against defendant No. 3 although the said defendant No. 3 has got no land in suit plot No. 125.

3. Defendant Nos. 1-2 and 25 contested the suit by filing separate written statements. Defendant Nos. 25, 28 and 29 also filed separate applications praying for 'saham.' Defendant No. 1 claimed that Nizamuddin had transferred .14 acre of land from Plot No. 124 and another .51 acre of land from plot Nos. 125 totaling .65 acre land to Chunni Jammader in 1936 by a registered sale deed keeping .84 acre of land of plot No. 125 in his possession. Chuni Jamader, subsequently sold his purchased land to Nuruddin and Asafuddin in 1941, the predecessors of Hanif and others, who amicably partitioned the same by partition deed dated 13th December, 1965. Defendant Nos. 2 and 25 also contested the suit by filing two separate written statements claiming dismissal of the suit. The defendant No. 2 claimed .22 acre of land from plot No. 125 and the defendant No. 25 claimed 14 kathas and odd land by way of purchase.

4. The trial court by judgment and order dated 25th August, 1991, decreed the suit in preliminary form against defendant Nos. 1-2, 25, 28 and 29 and ex-parte against others. The trial court held that “এই মর্মে বাদীকে নালিশী ‘খ’ তফিসিল বর্ণিত সম্পত্তিতে অবস্থিত .৬৫ শতাংশের কাতে .০২ শতাংশ ভূমি হইতে দেওয়ানী ৭৫/৮৫ মোকদ্দমায় ডিক্রী মূলে বেদখল করা বিবাদীগণ ক্ষমতা বর্হিভূত মর্মে ঘোষণা হইল।” The preliminary decree was drawn up accordingly. The defendant No. 1 thereafter preferred Title Appeal No. 377 of 1991 which appeal was dismissed by the judgment and order dated 29th June, 1992 and the said decree was affirmed on 5th July, 1994 by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2171 of 1992. This Division also affirmed the judgment of the High Court Division in Civil Petition No. 611 of 1994, and a review petition preferred by the defendant No. 1 being Civil Review Petition 32 of 1995 was also dismissed on 12th December, 1995. At the hearing of the review petition, it was argued on behalf of the defendant No. 1 that the plaintiff has no right or title in respect of .02 acre of land in C.S. plot No. 125. This Division repelled the contention observing. If the plaintiffs predecessors-in-interest had on saleable interest in the suit land at the time of their sale to the plaintiff then this basic fact ought to have been alleged and proved at the trial.'

5. Thereafter on the prayer of the plaintiff an Advocate Commissioner was appointed who submitted report in 18th August, 1996, against which the defendant No. 1 filed an objection. In the meantime, pursuant to an application moved on behalf of the defendant No. 1 under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the trial court dismissed the suit by order dated 30th November, 1991 and set aside the preliminary decree. Plaintiff then moved the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1 of 1997. The High Court Division set aside the order and restored the preliminary decree passed by the trial court by judgment dated 16th august, 1998. Thereafter the defendant No. 1 moved this Division in Civil Petition No. 1196 of 1998. This Division maintained the Judgment of the High Court Division. Thereafter the final decree was drawn up by the trial Court on 26th October, 1999.

6. Defendant No. 25, however, challenged the final decree in Civil Revision No. 4616 of 1999. The High Court Division discharged the rule. Thereafter, the heirs of defendant Nos. 1 and the defendant No. 2 preferred Title Appeal No. 619 of 2001 and the defendant No. 11 also preferred Title Appeal No. 20 of 2002 against the final decree. The plaintiff also filed a cross objection for partial modification of the final decree. The court of appeal below allowed the appeals and dismissed the cross-objection against which the plaintiff moved the High Court Division in Civil Revision Nos. 2825 and 2926 of 2003. The rules were discharged by judgment dated 7th June, 2011 against which the plaintiff moved this Division in Civil Petition Nos. 1163 and 1164 of 2005 which were also dismissed by judgment dated 18th February, 2007. Thereafter an Advocate Commissioner was appointed who submitted his report on 6th April, 2008 without giving the plaintiff a separate saham of .02 acre of land from plot No. 125, against which, the plaintiff filed an objection. The trial court rejected the objection and made the preliminary decree final. The plaintiff then preferred Title appeal No. 94 of 2009 which appeal was also dismissed. The High Court Division also affirmed the judgment of the court of appeal.

<u>7. There is no dispute that the plaintiff got a saham of .02 acre of land in plot No. 125. This preliminary decree has been affirmed by this Division. The dispute in respect of allotment of saham of .02 acre of land from C.S. Plot No. 125 in favour of the plaintiff has finally been adjudicated upon by the highest court and the same cannot be re-opened again. Though a preliminary decree passed in a partition suit is not a tentative decree, it is conclusive until it is reversed by the higher courts. The Court must carry out directions in preliminary decree and dispose of the suit completely particularly when such preliminary decree is affirmed by the apex court. It is only in case where after the preliminary decree and before the final decree, if subsequent events necessitate augmentation, reduction or nullification of allotment of shares, another preliminary decree may be drawn up. Subsequent events after preliminary decree that requires declaration of shares of parties afresh on account of death or transfer, modification of such decree is permissible. An Advocate Commissioner cannot travel beyond the preliminary decree while allotting saham to the parties. It is the fundamental principle that the Court or the Commissioner must carry out directions in preliminary decree and dispose of the suit completely. The proposals of the Advocate Commissioner beyond the preliminary decree is not binding upon the parties to the suit. An Advocate Commissioner cannot act formally as an arbitrator.</u>

8. In the case in hand the allotment of saham of .02 acre of land from plot No. 125 in favour of plaintiff was reopened at the instance of the defendant No. 1 and the basis is ext 10. This document was filed in the trial court and the trial court decreed the suit relying upon both oral and documentary evidence. So this document was before the courts below and the High Court Division at the time of confirming the preliminary decree dated 25th August, 1991. This partition deed was not a product of subsequent event after passing of the preliminary decree. Therefore this Division has committed a fundamental error in its judgment in civil petition Nos. 1163 and 1164 of 2005 in affirming the judgment of the High Court Division passed in civil Revision Nos. 2825 and 2826 of 2003, in which, the High Court Division observed that 'the .65 acre of land contained in admitted document, the partition deed (ext. 10) consisting of 0.14 acre of land of plot No. 124 and 0.51 acre of land of plot No. 125 and the said 0.65 acre land extend up to Mosque Gali and also has tallied with 'Kha' schedule land as per boundary.........

<u>9. The plaintiff was allotted .02 acre of land from plot No. 125 and the total partiable land in this plot is .65 acre. According to the plaintiff, he has been illegally dispossessed from this area of land and he has been able to establish this title over the said area of land and also dispossession in pursuance of a collusive decree. So there is no difficulty in giving saham of .02 acre of land to the plaintiff from plot No. 125. Mr. Rokanuddin Mahmud has also frankly conceded that the respondents have no objection if the plaintiff is allotted a saham of .02 acre of land from plot No. 125. Considering the facts and circumstances of the matter, we hold that the High Court Division has committed fundamental error in approving the commissioner's report, who has travelled beyond the preliminary decree.</u>

10. In view of the above and the admission of the learned counsel for the respondents, we direct the trial court to make necessary direction to the Advocate Commissioner to allot .02 acre of land from plot No. 125 in favour of the plaintiff. This petition is disposed of with the above observations and direction.

End.

lawyer:
Mr. S. N. Goswami, Advocate with Ms. Afsana Begum, Advocate ------ For the appellant. 
No one appears ------ For the respondents.
parties:
Sreemoti Rani Sinha ------ Appellant
Versus
Khokon Chandra Sinha and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Mr. Khizir Ahmed Choudhury, J:- The instant first appeal has been preferred against the judgment and order dated 15.11.2003 passed by the First Court of Joint District Judge, Naogaon and District Delegate in Probate Suit No.51 of 1997 filed under Section 299 of the Succession Act, 1925 dismissing the case. 

2. The case of the plaintiff was that her mother Shova Rani Roy, executed a 'Will' on 11.02.1991 corresponding to 27.10.1397 B.S. appointing her as legatee of the ‘Will’. The testator Shova Rani Roy died on 04.12.1996 leaving behind the daughter, plaintiff and others sons and  daughters.  

3. After her death, the plaintiff filed the instant case for Probate of the granted in her favour by deceased Shova Rani Roy. 

4. Notices have been issued upon the sons and daughters of Shova Rani Roy but none appeared to contest the suit inspite of service of summons upon them. 

5. Sreemoti Rani Sinha deposed as PW. 1 while Sreemoti Chandana who was the witness of the Probate dated 11.02.1991 deposed as PW.2. 

6. After hearing, learned Joint District Judge and District Delegate dismissed the case by holding that the 'Will' in question has been written in simple green paper and signature of PW.2 is not identical with her signature in the He further held that another witness of the 'Will' namely Koly has not been examined as witness. Learned District Delegate further held that documents of title of Shova Rani Roy the original owner was not produced and the 'Will' is not believable.

7. At the time of hearing of the appeal, the appellant filed an application under Order 41 Rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure for taking additional evidence in respect of deed of title dated 26.4.1984, 18.2.1968 annexing photocopies of those documents as Annexure A and A-1 . 

8. Mr. S.N. Goswami, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant submits that in a Probate case the Court is required only to consider whether the 'Will' was executed by the testator and it was attested by the witnesses. The Court need not decide question relating to title of the property. Mr. Goswami further contends that out of two witnesses mentioned in the 'Will' Sreemoti Chandana deposed as PW.2 who proved the execution of the 'Will'. He further submits that another witness of the 'Will' namely Koly was a declarant in the substantive application where she put her signature. 

9. Learned Advocate in support of his submissions referred the case of Saktirani Ghosh V. Gautam Ghosh reported in AIR 1979 NOC 46 (CAL.) wherein the following passage is relevant: "Under the law of Evidence one of the attesting witnesses' evidence is sufficient to prove the Will: as such non-calling of the doctor who is the other attesting witness could not be a ground for withholding the grant of probate of Will" He also referred the case of Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Comilla -Vs-Arun Kumar Chakraborty and others reported in 9 BLT(HCD) 192 wherein it has been stated that "In a Probate case, the Court is required only to consider whether the Will was duly executed by the testator and it was attested by witnesses. The Court cannot go into and decide any question relating to title in the disputed property." 

10. No one appears on behalf of the respondents. 

11. We have perused the documents and considered submissions of the learned Advocate for the appellant. 

12. In a Probate case the Court is required to consider whether the 'Will' is executed by the testator and it was attested by the witnesses. The Court is not required to consider to decide question of title. 

13. Upon perusal of the Annexures the documents of title submitted by the appellant's, which are registered instruments we found chain of title in favour of Shova Rani Roy. 

14. It appears that the District Delegate failed to appreciate the principle relating of grant of Probate. In the instant was PW1 recipient of the 'Will' has deposed stating that her mother executed the 'Will' and she herself proved the 'Will' in question. She further stated that her two sisters namely Sreemoti Chandana and Sreemoti Koly Rani were witnesses in the sister Chandana deposed as PW.2 and while deposing she stated that her mother wrote the 'Will' herself and executed the same. Hence the PWs proved execution of the 'Will'. It appears that Koly has put her signature in the declaration of substantive application being filed for Probate of the `Will'. Learned District Delegate committed error in not relying the evidence of those witnesses who are reliable and trustworthy. The District Delegate found that inspite of service of summons the sons of the propounder of 'Will' did not turn up to controvert the contention of the which also signifies that they are also not opposing the Will'. The test before the Court is, while determining the question as to whether the instrument produced before the Court is the last 'Will' of the testator, the Court is thereby deciding a solemn question and it must be fully satisfied that it had been validly executed by the testator. The test is satisfaction of judicial conscience. No hard and fast or inflexible rules can be laid down for appreciation of such evidence. From the proof of the signature of the deceased it will be presumed that the testator knew the provisions of the instrument he has signed and that presumption is liable to be rebutted by proof of suspicious circumstances. What is a suspicious circumstance is a question of fact depending on the peculiar circumstances of each case. Suspicious can never be allowed to prevail over evidence and circumstances. 

The findings and reasoning’s put forward by District Delegate is not tenable and not commensurate with the principles of grant of Probate and hence liable to be set aside. 

15. We find substance in the submission of the learned Advocate for the appellant. 

16. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed. The impugned judgment and order dated 15.11.2003 passed by the First Court of Joint District Judge, Naogaon and District Delegate in Probate Suit No.51 of 1997 is hereby set aside. The Probate case is allowed. Learned District Delegate is directed to obtain a valuation statement from the collector ascertaining the value of the subject matter and to realize to due Court fees from the petitioner within four months from the date of receipt of this order. 

17. Let a copy of this judgment be sent to the concerned Court. 

18. Send down the lower Court's record. 

End.

lawyer:
MI Farooqui with Md Ruhul Quddus and Nazneen Nahar, Advocates—For the Petitioner.
AF Hassan Ariff, with MA Sobhan, Advocates—For Opposite Party Nos. 1-5
parties:
Abu Aslam (Md) Advocate, Member, Rajshahi District Bar Association ------ Petitioner
vs 
Rajshahi University, Rajshahi being represented by its Vice Chancellor and others ------ Respondents.
full_judgment:
Opposite party Nos. 1-5 were called upon to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 14-7-04 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Rajshahi in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 50/2004 allowing the appeal and setting aside the order of temporary injunction dated 23-6-2004 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Rajshahi Sadar in Other Class Suit No. 87/2004 should not be set aside.

2. Facts giving rise to this Rule, in short, is that the petitioner as plaintiff instituted the suit for declaration that the appointments of 546 employees (3rd & 4th class) are illegal, collusive, malafide and against the interest of Rajshahi University and for permanent injunction restraining the defendant Nos. 1-5 from confirming the said appointments and also prayed for temporary injunction restraining them from giving salaries and assigning any duties to the said employees.

3. The plaintiff-petitioner stated in his plaint, inter alia, that the plaintiff is a Lawyer and a member of Rajshahi District Bar Association. Rajshahi University is a national institution and being a citizen of the country he is obliged to protect its interest as well as the interest of the nation and hence filed the suit in public interest as a conscious citizen. The plaintiff alleged that the Rajshahi University (defendant No. 1) is an autonomous body and its administration, appointments, promotions and control of all teachers and employees and admission of its students are regulated under the Rajshahi University Act as well as the notifications and circulars of the University Grants Commission, hereinafter referred as UGC, that the UGC by a circular dated 28-5-03 declared that their should be no appointment in excess of the budget of the University and in appointing its teachers, officers and employees the guidelines of the UGC must be followed, that no appointment under Master Roll on the basis of daily payment should be given from 1-6-2003 and in case of appointment of employees its 50% posts should be filled from the sons/daughters heirs of the retired employees. But the Rajshahi University Authority illegally appointed 546 persons as 3rd and 4th Class employees on 15-4-2004 in an unprecedented manner and without following the established rules to fulfil personal and political interest of defendant Nos. 2-5 and against the interest of Rajshahi University (defendant No. 1). It is further stated that there was no necessity of such huge employees and no demand from the concerned departments for such appointments even in some cases there was no post and there was no public notice and advertisement for such appointments. It has been further stated that the Teachers Association of Rajshahi University observed strike in protest of the aforesaid illegal appointments and educational environment of the University has been disturbed and the University would suffer a loss of Taka 1,25,00,000 every year for such illegal appointments causing unnecessary huge financial burden and expenditure of the University striking at its financial strength to exist, etc. Hence, the plaintiff has thus filed the suit for public interest and to protect the said national institution. The plaintiff-petitioner also filed an application under Order XXXIX, rule 1 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure on the similar fact along with relevant documents filed by way of First for an order of temporary injunction against defendant Nos. 1-5 restraining them from confirming of their appointments and from giving salaries and assigning duties to them till disposal of the suit.

4. The defendant-opposite parties 1-5 and 7, 10, 23, 28, 32, 35, 41, 42, 44, 52, 53, 54, 56, 60 and 64 appeared and filed two sets of written objections. Defendant-opposite party Nos. 1-5 contested the application denying the material averments of the application and stating in their written objections, in short, inter alia, that the plaintiff has no prima facie case, the balance of convenience and inconvenience is against him, that the restriction on appointment was withdrawn by the UGC on 22-12-2003 and restriction imposed by the Government was also withdrawn on 8-1-2004 by two separate circulars that in a meeting held on 22-3-2004 a decision for appointment of 327 4th Class employees on the daily basis was approved following due process and a decision for 219 3rd Class employees against vacant and non-created posts was approved on 24-3-04 by a duly constituted committee. Their further case is that said 546 (3rd and 4th class) employees were permitted to work in the interest of the University and already joined in their respective places of works and those employees along with their family members would be thrown in the street if they are removed or disturbed in their employment in any manner. They further stated that the internal administration and management of the University, its Departments. Halls and Faculties would be seriously affected, disturbed and interfered if the injunction is granted. They contends that the appointments have been made in good faith, in due process of law and for the interest of the University for which the plaintiff would not suffer any loss, etc the other set of written objections contends, inter alia, in short, that these answering defendants were not involved in appointing the said 546 employees in any manner and it was done violating the rules of the University and even there was no demand for such appointments from the respective offices departments and Falls and that the Chairman Council in its meeting dated 19-4-04 expressed their concern against such illegal appointments and demanded withdrawal of the newly appointed employees. Their further case is that since the appointments have been made excluding the employees who were already, in work, it created embarrassment of the Chairmen of different departments, etc.

5. The learned Senior Assistant Judge. Sadar by his order dated 23-6-04 allowed the said application on contest and granted temporary injunction restraining the defendant Nos. 1-5 from assigning any duties and giving salaries to said 546 employees and confirming their appointments on daily basis. That the defendant-opposite party Nos. 1-5 being aggrieved by the aforesaid order of temporary injunction filed Miscellaneous, Appeal No. 50 of 2004 before the learned District Judge, Rajshahi. The Miscellaneous Appeal was heard by the learned Additional District Judge 2nd Court, Rajshahi and the same was allowed by the impugned judgment and order dated 14-7-04 setting aside and vacating the order of temporary injunction passed by the trial Court. Hence this Rule at the instance of the plaintiff-petitioner.

6. The defendant-opposite party Nos. 1-5 have opposed and contested the Rule by filing a counter-affidavit.

7. Trial Court allowing the application for temporary injunction observed and found that all appointments of the University were barred till 22-12-2003 and the bar was withdrawn by a circular of the UGC dated 22-12-2003 and the restrictions imposed by the Government was also withdrawn on 8-1-04 by two separate circulars allowing to make necessary appointment as per prevailing rule and procedure. But the proposal of appointment of 546 employees was not communicated to the Government through UGC for approval nor the Government or the UGC approved the same. A new set of work-charged appointments were made on daily basis in Master Roll defying and without fulfilling the terms of the circular dated 4-11-1997 issued by the Registrar of the University malafide and illegally in order to remove the existing sets of employees of the same nature, that the appointments were made whimsically which is clear from the office order dated 31-5-04 of the defendant No. 2, the Vice-Chancellor of Rajshahi University, that the Rajshahi University Teachers Association in its meeting held on 20-4-04 demanded withdrawal of appointments of the said employees. The trial Court also found that there was neither any requirement nor demand nor proposal from the departmental heads nor there was any proposal from the Planning Committee of the University for such unprecedented huge number of appointments at a time, that there was no advertisement or notification in any dailies for such appointments and the appointments were made by the defendant Nos. 2 and 3 secretly by misusing their power to make the University a 'Lilla Boarding' and against the principle of natural justice on nepotism and favouritism instead of following the rules and procedures.
